statement:
**Source-defined terminology (not inherited hypotheses):** A ring $A$ is **w-contractible** iff every faithfully flat weakly étale map $A\to B$ admits an $A$-algebra retraction. A **pro-étale covering** of $T$ is a family of weakly étale maps whose images admit finite affine-open refinements covering every affine open of $T$.

Let $T = \Spec(A)$ be an affine scheme. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is w-contractible, and
\item every pro-\'etale covering of $T$ can be refined by
a Zariski covering of the form $T = \coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i$.
\end{enumerate}

proposed_correction: With S and listed sites as setup, conclude (1) every U has a covering by a weakly contractible V; and (2) if U is quasi-compact V can be chosen affine, without assuming (1) upfront.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-weakly-contractible-cover}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The pro-\'etale sites
$\Sch_\proetale$, $S_\proetale$, $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$
have the following property: for any object
$U$ there exists a covering $\{V \to U\}$ with $V$ a
weakly contractible object. If $U$ is quasi-compact, then we
may choose $V$ affine and weakly contractible.
